subject: Scaling add-on enquiry — tierless rollup & volume credit mechanics
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@novapower.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@novapower.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-contract capacity add-on and pricing options

Hi Stephanie / Jordan,

Hope you’re both well. We’ve seen an unexpected spike in inference consumption for a pilot we’re accelerating — roughly +40% over committed monthly units for the next 6 months. Our finance sponsor is asking whether we can do a mid-contract add-on that: 1) gives us a meaningful unit discount on the added volume, and 2) co-terms the added capacity to our existing renewal date (Nov 30, 2028).

Questions up front:
- Do you support a blended/rollup-style discount for mid-term top-ups versus a one-time uplift credit?
- What packaging options (true-up vs. reserved add-on) preserve our current SLAs?
- Procurement will need a pricing PDF and a quick total-cost impact calc for tomorrow’s budget meeting.

We’re also tight on procurement windows — can you accommodate net-60 invoicing and vendor registration details?

Thanks — if it helps I can put Max (legal) and procurement on a short call this week.

Best,
Elena
Elena Park
Head of Platform, NovaPower AI
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@novapower.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jul 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-contract capacity add-on and pricing options

Elena — thanks for the note and the heads-up. Short answers: yes, we can do both a blended rollup (keeps units priced on a blended effective rate for the remainder of the term) and a one-time uplift credit. Which is better depends on whether you want an ongoing lower per-unit price for the remainder of the contract or a single offsetted charge today.

High-level proposal for your procurement meeting (attached PDF + calculator):
- Option A (Blended rollup): We roll the incremental 40% into a tierless rollup that re-prices total monthly units at a blended effective discount of 12% on the increment for the remaining 4.3 months (until co-term). Requires a short amendment and PO.
- Option B (One-time credit): One-off invoice credit equal to 10% of the projected incremental spend for the 6-month window. Keeps current contract untouched.

Operational notes:
- SLA: Both options preserve existing SLAs. If you want dedicated reserved units we can provide via a dedicated pool (longer lead time).
- Billing: We can support net-60 on a case-by-case basis; procurement will need a vendor addendum and W-9 (I’ve cc’d Lauren to help with vendor setup).

I attached: nova_addon_pricing_v1.pdf and an editable volume_calculator.xlsx. If you’re free, I can run a 20-minute call today at 2pm PT to walk procurement/legal through numbers.

—
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0183
From: Elena Park <elena@novapower.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Max Chen <max.chen@novapower.ai>, Procurement <procurement@novapower.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Jul 2028 08:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-contract capacity add-on and pricing options

Thanks Stephanie — the materials are helpful. A couple of procurement constraints:
- They require a single-line PO and vendor registration fields completed before we can accept amendments.
- Net-60 is preferred (they push that for cloud vendors).
- If we take Option A, finance wants to see the blended rate as an effective USD/unit over the remaining term (not % only).

Legal (Max) asked whether any of these options trigger additional data handling clauses or change data residency — answer?

We can do the 2pm PT call — I’m adding Max and procurement into the calendar invite.

On the SLA/reserved pool: is there a price difference for moving a portion of the uplift to reserved (guaranteed capacity) vs keeping it as elastic hosted usage?

Appreciate the quick turnaround,
Elena
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jul 2028 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Mid-contract capacity add-on and pricing options — internal

Internal — forwarding NovaPower thread. Key asks: 40% uplift for ~6 months, procurement wants net-60, legal will review data residency and vendor registration. They prefer blended rollup but need USD/unit impact.

Quick decisions I need:
- Discount cap for blended rollup we can approve without finance sign-off? I suggested 12% in the client-facing PDF but haven’t committed. Is 12% within our standard mid-contract uplift guardrails for a customer at this scale?
- Reserved pool premium: what’s a defensible premium if they move 30% of the uplift into a reserved capacity bucket?

Ben — can you confirm margin at 12% blended for remaining term and whether we can stretch to 15% if Jordan pushes for the close?
Lauren — please prep vendor registration template + W-9 so we can send procurement immediately.

I’ll be on the call with them at 2pm PT. We should have a short triage and finalize numbers by 1:30.

—
Stephanie
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@novapower.ai>, Max Chen <max.chen@novapower.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>, Procurement <procurement@novapower.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Jul 2028 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Final offer — tierless rollup with co-term path + mutual action plan

Elena / Max — great to chat earlier this week. Per our discussion, here’s the updated, executable offer and next steps: 

Offer (clean execution path):
- Tierless rollup (preferred): We’ll reprice total monthly units for the remainder of the contract period using a blended effective rate that yields ~10% savings on the incremental 40% uplift if NovaPower signs the amendment and issues a PO by Aug 10. That blended USD/unit is shown in the attached PDF and the calculator.
- Alternate (one-time): 6% one-time credit applied to the invoice for the 6-month uplift window if you prefer to avoid an amendment.
- Reserved option: If you convert 30% of the uplift into reserved capacity, the reserved premium is +4% on that portion but we guarantee throughput and lower variance on tail latency.

Operational items:
- Net-60 invoicing: approved for this deal; Lauren will send the vendor addendum and W-9.
- Data residency: no changes to data handling or residency — existing contract remains in effect. Legal can sign the short addendum (we don’t need a full SOW).

Next steps (mutual action plan):
1) NovaPower issues PO for amendment + confirms option (rollup or one-time) by Aug 10.
2) Redwood prepares amendment and DocuSign envelope (Lauren/Jordan).
3) Legal review window: Max to confirm redlines within 5 business days.
4) Go-live of pricing adjustments: immediate upon countersignature; billable on next invoice cycle.

Attachments: nova_addon_pricing_v1.pdf, volume_calculator.xlsx, mutual_action_plan.docx
DocuSign (placeholder): https://docusign.com/envelope/0AB12CDE34FG5678
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/NW-4371

If that all looks good we’ll convert the pricing and get Lauren to raise the vendor paperwork. Happy to jump back on a quick call to walk the PO format.

Best,
